_meta.purpose: Human decisions that must survive a registry rebuild. build-registry.mjs regenerates registry.json from OSM + crawls every run, so anything recorded only there is lost on the next build. This file is the durable layer.
_meta.rule: Only a human writes here. Nothing in this file is inferred, and every entry carries the evidence that justified it.

notBrewery._note: Excluded from all brewery queries but deliberately KEPT as records, with their OSM ids intact — a later fetch-osm-breweries run would otherwise re-add them silently. `venueKind` is what downstream filtering should read.

bungalow.why: Pours Samuel Adams, Creemore, Stiegl, Sapporo — no own beer

daniel-o-connell-s-irish-pub.why: Irish pub; pours Guinness. OSM website tag also wrong (points at filsdiner.ca)

irene-s.why: Pours Guinness, Creemore, Moosehead, Beau's and others

jack-s-gastropub.why: Pours Heineken, Land Shark, Smirnoff Ice. Also rebranded — domain now thegoosekitchenandbar.com

morty-s-pub.why: Pours Molson Canadian, Coors Light, Bud Light. NOTE: has a live store API whose products classified as offers:sour — a pub menu read as a brewery catalog

pheasant-plucker.why: Pours Guinness. NOTE: carries offers (pilsner-lager, amber-red, hazy-ipa, pale-ale) crawled from its PUB MENU, not its own range

real-sports-bar-and-grill.why: Sports bar; pours Guinness, Carlsberg, Heineken, Molson

the-overtime-pub.why: Pours Kronenbourg, Michelob Ultra, Bud Light, Carlsberg

forty-creek-distillery.why: Distillery. The brewery=* test structurally cannot catch this — it pours its own product, so there is no third-party brand list

joe-hot-cold-coffee.why: Coffee shop. Domain now redirects to thegrove.rocks/joe

eataly-toronto.why: Italian food hall, not a brewery

the-forty.why: The Forty Public House, Grimsby. Domain now redirects to its Facebook page. A pub, not a brewery — missed by the brewery=* test because OSM records no tap list for it.

closed._note: status: closed. Domain loss alone is evidence, not proof — each of these also has no corroborating signal (no live store, no crawled catalog, no recent OSM survey).

batch.why: batchtoronto.com now serves catscradleboutique.com, a boutique. No other signal.

fenelon-falls-brewing-co.why: fenelonfallsbrewing.com listed for sale on HugeDomains. No other signal.

evergreen-craft-ales.why: evergreencraftales.com redirects to linktt4dku.website, a parked spam domain.

gather.why: gatherbrewery.ca now serves grayartglass.com. The glassworks continued; the brewery did not.

stone-city-ales.why: Confirmed by Corey 2026-08-18. 275 Princess St, Kingston is now Something in the Water's Kingston Taproom — somethingbrewing.ca lists that exact address. stonecityales.com serves an unrelated UK firm.

manitoulin-brewery.why: Confirmed by Corey 2026-08-25. Closure announced 2026-04-09 after ~12 years — CBC, CTV, Northern Ontario Business, The Manitoulin Expositor all report it; Google's knowledge layer now says 'permanently closed'. Own domain still serves, which is why check-sites never caught it — found by the wide-harvest liveness probe.
manitoulin-brewery.note: Announcement mentioned prospective buyers; if it reopens under new ownership that is a NEW decision, not a revert of this one.

websiteFix._note: The brewery moved and is trading; our recorded domain was stale. Verified live before writing.

merit.why: Confirmed by Corey 2026-08-18. meritbrewing.ca returns 200 with a working Shopify store; the old .com is listed on HugeDomains. OSM was also surveyed on the ground 2025-06-01.

notes.something-in-the-water-brewing-co: Two locations: Liberty Village, Toronto (the one this record holds) and the Kingston taproom at 275 Princess St that was Stone City Ales. The registry is one-record-per-brewery, so the Kingston site is currently unrepresented.

falsePositive._note: check-sites.mjs flagged these as dead. They are not. Recorded here so a future run of that script cannot re-flag them without a human looking again.

beyond-the-pale.why: beyondthepale.ca redirects to btpshop.ca, which is THEIR OWN shop — not a domain that changed hands. Their store API answers live with 41 products, the catalog crawled fine, and OSM has hours. Open.
